interface.name: cutefish_surface_blur_v1

description.summary: compositor background blur for translucent surfaces

interface.description:
A Cutefish extension inspired by Chromium ui::Layer backdrop filters. This is not a ChromeOS wire protocol. Requests modify pending wl_surface state, applied atomically on wl_surface.commit, including synchronized subsurface commits. Blur samples content behind the surface, before the client buffer is blended. The compositor chooses sigma and filter quality; clients paint their own translucent tint. No additional surface role is assigned. The effect is available to both toplevels and popups.
The same rectangle can carry a glass material instead, which refracts and lights the backdrop rather than only blurring it.
A client that draws a body of any other outline - a popup with an arrow, say - describes that outline with set_shape, and the blur, the window outline and the shadow follow it.

entry.name: invalid_geometry
entry.summary: invalid blur rectangle, radius, shape or glass parameter

request.name: destroy
request.description: Existing surface state is unchanged. Use unset before committing to remove an effect. Surface destruction discards all its blur state.

request.name: set

description.summary: set a rounded background blur rectangle

request.description: Coordinates and radius are surface-local logical pixels, independent of buffer scale and transform. Width and height must be positive; radius must be nonnegative and is clamped to half the smaller dimension. Output is clipped to the surface content and rounded rectangle. Input sampling extends beyond that rectangle to avoid blur edge artifacts. A subsequent set replaces the pending rectangle.

description.summary: disable blur on the next surface commit

request.name: set_glass

description.summary: turn the blur rectangle into a glass lens

request.description:
Refracts the backdrop through a rounded lens shaped by the rectangle and radius of the most recent set request, then lights it. Without such a rectangle the request has no effect. The material starts at the compositor defaults; set_glass_material, set_glass_lighting and set_glass_tint override parts of it and may be sent in any order, before or after this request. All of it is pending surface state.
Glass replaces the plain blur for this surface. Clients should not paint a translucent tint of their own on top of it; use set_glass_tint so the tint sits under the highlights instead of over them.

request.name: unset_glass

description.summary: go back to plain blur on the next commit

request.description: The blur rectangle is unaffected. Material parameters are retained, so a later set_glass restores them.

request.name: set_glass_material

description.summary: set the optical properties of the glass

request.description:
blur_sigma softens the backdrop before it is refracted; it is much smaller than the plain blur radius because a heavily blurred backdrop leaves nothing for the lens to bend. bevel is the width of the roll-off band, the visible lip of the glass, in surface-local logical pixels; it is clamped to half the smaller side of the rectangle and falls back to the rectangle's corner radius when zero. depth is the height of the glass surface above its back face: against the bevel width it decides how steeply the surface turns over at the edge. profile is the superellipse exponent of the surface, so low values give a dome and high values a flat top with a roll-off so sharp the lip stops bending light over a visible width. displacement is the length of the refracted ray inside the glass, in logical pixels, and may be negative to bend the other way. chroma splits red from blue as a fraction of the resulting offset.
Negative blur_sigma, bevel, depth, profile or chroma, and an index of refraction below one, are invalid geometry.

request.name: set_glass_lighting

description.summary: set the lighting of the glass

request.description:
light_angle is in degrees, measured from the surface-local x axis with y growing downwards. sheen brightens the whole surface by how much it faces the light and specular_intensity adds a mirror highlight, which on a panel reads as plastic and is normally left at zero. ambient_occlusion darkens the inside of the edge over ambient_occlusion_radius logical pixels. Intensities are fractions of full brightness and are combined with a screen blend, so they brighten towards white rather than clipping.
The material draws no edge of its own unless set_glass_rim asks for one: otherwise the hairline around a rounded body belongs to the compositor's window outline.
A negative radius, intensity or shininess is invalid geometry.

request.name: set_glass_tint
request.description: A straight-alpha colour mixed over the refracted backdrop, under the highlights. Components are clamped to the 0 to 1 range.

entry.name: cubic_to
entry.summary: followed by two control points and the end point

request.name: set_shape

description.summary: replace the rounded rectangle by an outline

request.description:
The outline the client paints its body in. It takes the place of the rounded rectangle of set: the blur is masked by it, and the window outline and the shadow are drawn around it. It is clipped to that rectangle, which must still be set for any effect to show.
path is an array of int32 values: a path_command followed by its points, each point an x and a y in wl_fixed, surface-local logical pixels. The filled area follows the nonzero winding rule. An empty array removes the shape, the same as unset_shape.
With the glass material the lens stays on the rectangle and the shape masks it instead of replacing it. The shape is then not clipped to the rectangle; the part outside it is flat tinted glass. It is pending surface state; a subsequent set_shape replaces it.
An unknown command, a command cut short, a path that does not start with move_to or an array longer than 4096 values is invalid geometry.

description.summary: go back to the rounded rectangle on the next commit

request.name: set_glass_saturation

description.summary: set the saturation of the refracted backdrop

request.description: Applied to the backdrop before the tint. 1 leaves it unchanged, 0 turns it grey and values above 1 make it more vivid. A negative value is invalid geometry. Pending surface state, like the rest of the material.

request.name: set_glass_rim

description.summary: light the edge of the glass

request.description: A thin edge drawn by the material itself: where it faces up or down it is lit in the colour of the backdrop behind it, and along the sides it is shaded. intensity runs from 0, no rim, to 1 and is clamped to that range; a negative value is invalid geometry. While the rim is on the compositor draws no window outline around the body, so the two do not stack. Pending surface state, like the rest of the material.

request.name: set_over_subsurfaces

description.summary: blur the surface's subsurfaces placed below it

request.description: A second rounded blur rectangle, drawn after the subsurfaces placed below the surface and before the surface itself, so it blurs them together with what lies behind the whole surface tree: a translucent panel the surface paints over content one of its subsurfaces below it shows, such as a video or a terminal drawn by the GPU. Coordinates and radius are surface-local logical pixels, as for set; width and height must be positive and radius nonnegative, and it is clamped to half the smaller dimension. The compositor chooses the blur as for set; the client paints its own tint. Independent of set and the glass material. Pending surface state; a subsequent set_over_subsurfaces replaces it.

description.summary: remove the blur over the subsurfaces on the next commit
